title: Quasi-compactness of the section component locus over an affine base
statement: Let (g:P\to T) be flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], with (P\to T) quasi-compact and quasi-separated, and let (sigma:T\to P) be a section of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume every fibre is geometrically reduced [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], (T) is affine [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and (C\subseteq P) is the union of the connected components [def-weil-connected-scheme] of fibres containing the section. Then (C) is quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme].

lean.note: Exact published declaration. Its compactness conclusion is the set of points lying in the connected component of the section in each fibre, i.e. the node’s locus C. The theorem is stronger than the node’s hypotheses: it only requires local finite presentation, quasi-compactness, and quasi-separatedness/compactness instances; the node’s flatness and geometrically reduced fibres are extra assumptions, and an affine base supplies the compactness and quasi-separatedness instances required by the declaration.
